items: map the posterior calyces, renal pelvis, ureter, and level of obstruction.
a posterior mid- or lower-pole calyx provides a straight papillary tract with lower vascular risk.
approach through this relatively avascular posterolateral plane; target the calyceal papilla and avoid direct pelvic or infundibular puncture.
map the pleura and lung, colon, bowel, right-sided liver, and left-sided spleen.
favor a subcostal route when feasible; a higher supracostal path carries greater pleural risk.
side, obstruction level, urgency, antibiotics, and the intended drainage endpoint.
use ultrasound and Doppler to find a safe posterior calyx and avoid vessels or adjacent organs.
puncture the central papilla under image guidance; confirm urine return before gentle contrast.
send cultures promptly and avoid pressurizing an infected system.
advance into the pelvis or ureter and stabilize the wire before dilation.
dilate the tract and form the locking loop fully within the collecting system.
use gentle contrast, connect to gravity, secure the tube, and document the output.
the key acute risk in infected obstruction. Give antibiotics, limit contrast and manipulation, and escalate rigors or hypotension.
use a posterior calyx; heavy or persistent hematuria with instability suggests vascular injury.
avoid an unnecessarily high route and keep pleura, colon, bowel, liver, and spleen outside the tract.
optimize ultrasound or CT guidance rather than repeatedly redirecting blindly.
stabilize the wire before dilation; never advance against resistance or suspected extravasation.

blocks.title: Routine orders
items: Diet - Outpatient: order regular diet. Inpatient: notify primary team diet is okay.
Vital signs per unit routine.
Tylenol 650 mg PRN.
Drain flush: 10 mL BID while admitted, 10 mL daily while outpatient.

blocks.title: Anticoagulation to resume
items: Warfarin: 24 hours.
IV unfractionated heparin: 6-8 hours.
Enoxaparin: 12 hours.
DOACs: Typically 24 hours; confirm agent and renal function.
Clopidogrel: 75 mg dose - 6 hours; 300-600 mg loading dose - 24 hours.
Aspirin: 24 hours.
Restart after hemostasis is confirmed; individualize timing for procedure-specific or patient-specific exceptions.

blocks.title: Drain care
items: Gravity drainage unless otherwise ordered.
Transient hematuria is expected; escalate persistent heavy bleeding, obstructing clots, hypotension, or falling Hgb.

blocks.title: Discharge - if outpatient
items: Discharge order with medication reconciliation - 30 minutes.
After visit summary: .IRAVSPCN1.

blocks.title: Follow up
items: Routine exchange/check in 3 months unless infection, malfunction, or urology plan requires earlier follow-up.
